A sick man wants to give away his property, is advised, buys land, makes the gift and dies, and the Sages uphold it. Several actions and a resolution.
A disagreement in which R. Yohanan is grieved and R. Elazar, seeing his distress, finds a consoling teaching. Conflict, an emotional reaction and a response.
A man brings a get to R. Yishmael and gets a ruling. After he leaves, R. Elai challenges it and R. Yishmael silences him.
A widow's demands before Rav Yosef, ending in her retort about silk. Almost entirely speech and rulings, with some conflict.
Hama pays Avimi's debt, the creditors refuse to return the document, and R. Abbahu rules. An incident with a ruling.
A divorcee comes before Shmuel, Rav Dimi tests her with her son, the baby recognises her, and she is ordered to take him. A full incident.
A general legal ruling about kidnapped women debated in dialogue; no event that happened is narrated.
Eyewitness incident: a woman came before Ameimar claiming a tenth of the estate, her brothers responded, and Ameimar's silence served as his ruling.
Rabbi Elazar b. R. Yosei testified once, and the court nearly elevated a slave to priesthood because of it: an incident with a consequence.
A legal enactment, a harmonization, and Abaye's mother's teachings on ages; no narrated event.
A Jew and a gentile walking together: the gentile tries a trick, the Jew sighs but keeps up, and they have a pointed exchange. Actions plus conflict.
The prince's household seized an orphans' maidservant, the judges approved it, and Rabbi Abba confronted them: an incident with a ruling and conflict.
Rav Shimi bar Ashi's ruse to irrigate Abaye's fields, and Abaye's reaction of refusing that year's produce.
A witness tells R. Tarfon about the lion-hearted traveler's deed and later death, and R. Tarfon permits the wife to remarry: an incident followed by a ruling.
A widow claims her ketubah, the orphans object to how she is dressed, she puts on all her clothes, and Ravina rules: an incident with a ruling.
Rav Pappa and Rav Huna were about to act on a baraita, an old woman stopped them, Rav Pappi rebuked them, and they admitted they had forgotten: an event with conflict and change.
A halakhic statement and Shmuel's reply when it was reported to him; speech only, with no event and no conflict narrated.
Dama ben Netina's mother tears his cloak, hits him and spits at him, and he does not shame her. He is a post-biblical figure, so it is in scope.
A halakhic question and answer between Rava bar Rav Hanan and Abaye; no event.
The steward argues the orphans' case before Abaye, wins step by step, and Abaye praises him: an incident with rulings.
A gentile's threat reveals a killing; the widow goes to Abaye, who defers, is sent to Rav Yosef, and Rav Yosef rules: an incident with a ruling.
Funerals were so costly that families abandoned their dead; Rabban Gamliel chose a plain burial, and the people's practice changed.
Ilfa hangs from a ship's mast and stakes his life on a challenge, and an old man comes and tests him.
Ravina recited the blessing at the betrothal, sure the match would hold, and the other family backed out: an act with an outcome.
Nehunya's daughter falls into a cistern, R. Hanina ben Dosa predicts she will be saved, and she is rescued. Segment 4 is later commentary (R-B4).
The incident is only alluded to in support of a ruling, and not enough of it is given.
A poor man demands rich food from Rava, and Rava's long-absent sister arrives with exactly that food: an event that resolves the conflict.
A one-line precedent (they forced the master to free her) cited for legal analysis; not enough of the incident is given.
Rabbi ruled (or was about to rule), Perata objected, and Rabbi reversed or withheld the ruling: an incident with change, told in two versions.
Two sages' habitual practices and their consequence; no one-time event follows the custom.
A yevama spits before the halitza, R. Ami rules, R. Abba bar Memel challenges him, then goes out, checks, and finds R. Ami was right.
A man whose betrothed died came before the sages, who ruled, and Rav Hiyya objected: an incident followed by a ruling and response.
Rav's parting from R. Hiyya, his contrary wife, and his son Hiyya reversing the requests, with discovery and response: a full narrative.
A legal objection citing a mishna dispute; no narrated event.
R. Hanina bar Pappi is enticed, afflicts himself, is healed by her magic, flees to a dangerous bathhouse and is questioned the next day: multiple events with conflict.
Rabba bar bar Hana gave Rav money to buy land and Rav bought it for himself: an incident with conflict; the Gemara's justification is commentary but the incident stands.

An eyewitness account of Nakdimon's daughter gathering barley from horses' hooves, with R. Elazar's response in a verse; something happened to someone and a person responded, though it is close to the one-line eyewitness edge.
R. Zeira's sermon gets him pelted with etrogim; Rava preaches, is carried on silk, preaches again and answers the crowd: events and reactions.
A groom complains, the bride protests, Rabban Gamliel has the cloth washed, finds blood and rules: an incident with actions and resolution.
A brother seeks to disqualify the yevama, and the passage is mainly a negotiating dialogue with conflict but little action beyond speech.

A man betroths with a stone, Rav Hisda appraises it, the man's mother protests and Rav Hisda rejects her claim: an incident, a ruling and a challenge; the first case in [2] is a bare examination wrapped in Gemara commentary.
A purely verbal exchange of boasts between an Amorite and an Israelite: speech with some conflict and no action.
The Nezonya elders boycott, Rav Hamnuna is sent to ban them, is stumped and mocked, and returns to Rav Hisda; the baraita citation that follows is the Gemara's legal material.
Legal discussion of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel on nursing vows; no event.
After a habitual frame, one day Satan appears as a woman, R. Akiva climbs the palm and is stopped: a one-time event with conflict.
Abaye's custom is followed by a one-time incident: the rabbis fail to stand, he rebukes them and they answer.
A legal inference and objection; no narrated event.
A man set a deadline, was blocked by the ferry, shouted across, and Shmuel ruled: an incident with a ruling; [3] is Gemara commentary.
A man sold himself to gladiators and came before R. Ami: the start of an incident whose plea and ruling continue in the next segment.
Mishna listing a wife's duties; normative law, no event.

King Yannai's feast, Elazar ben Po'ira's incitement, the accusation and the killing of the Sages: a full narrative about a post-biblical king, in scope; [6] carries a Gemara interjection but completes the baraita.
A man comes before R. Yoshiya, who compels him to authorize a get and sends the elders to hide and write it: an incident with actions.
R. Hama bar Bisa returns after twelve years, meets his son unknowingly, is distressed, and stands before him at home: a full narrative.
Rabba abrogates a debt and the debtor leaves; Abaye coaches the debtor, he returns, and Rabba takes the money and remarks: multiple events with change.
A man ordered ten to write a get, the signing was delayed, and he came before R. Yehoshua ben Levi, who ruled: an incident followed by a ruling.
Mar Ukva, tormented, writes to R. Elazar, who counsels patience, and the tormentor Geneiva is put in a neck iron: events with conflict and resolution; [5] is a separate legal query.
Onkelos (post-biblical) raises Titus, Balaam and Jesus by necromancy in sequence before converting; a full narrative. Segment 7 is R. Elazar's separate concluding dictum on Kamtza.
Rav Zevid's daughter-in-law rebels holding a garment; the sages rule and Rav Gamda accuses them of flattery — an incident, a ruling and a conflict.
A report that Rabbi lay ill in Tzippori with a burial place ready, followed by the Gemara's harmonization; nothing happens and no one responds.
Rav Sheshet exposes the Exilarch's servants, survives their plots with the bone and the pit, and explains to Rav Hisda — a full multi-action narrative with conflict.
An incident: a woman rebelled, Mar Zutra compelled her, and R. Hanina of Sura was born of the union — an event, a ruling and a consequence.
After the habitual frame of R. Tarfon's service to his mother, a one-time event follows: he boasts in the study hall and is rebuked.
Rav Kahana gathers and eats dates, the owner objects, and Rav Kahana responds — a concrete incident with a response.
A habitual practice (bringing gifts to a wife who aggravates him) and a dialogue with Rav; there is conflict, but no one-time event beyond the speech.
Orphans come before Rava, he rules, the sages challenge him and he defends himself — an incident followed by a ruling.
A pauper demands luxury food from Rava, and Rava's sister providentially arrives with exactly that; there are actions, conflict and a resolution.
R. Eliezer finds no quorum and frees his slave to complete it: a problem arises and he takes a responding action, even though it is cited as an objection.
The bride dies, the families' lineage is examined, and the new match leads to the son's impatience and his father's response — a multi-event narrative.
A report that R. Zeira was avoiding Rav Yehuda, followed by Rav Yehuda's dictum; nothing happens within the passage.
Rav Pappa forces Yehuda bar Mareimar to enter, and his silence makes Abba of Sura write over all his property — actions, misunderstanding and resolution.
Purely speech — R. Yannai rebukes Rav Hanina's ruling and sends him out — but with clear conflict.
A man who sold himself to gladiators asks to be redeemed; R. Ami agrees, the sages object, and he refuses — an incident with a ruling and a reversal.
Actual cases in which a man willed a dowry or wine to his daughter, prices changed, and a rabbi ruled — the incident-plus-ruling shape of R-C0.
Two rabbis stand as R. Shimon bar Abba passes, and he objects to the honor — an action and a response.
A dialogue between an Amorite and a resident of the Land of Israel with no action, though it carries an accusation and a rebuttal.
A man asks Rav about his lineage and then asks for Rav's daughter; Rav refuses, the man persists, and Rav's gaze kills him.
A baraita's legal case and its explanation; hypothetical law, not an event.
Shmuel's instruction to gather ten men is cited as a speech act to illustrate publicizing a halakha; there is no event or conflict.
A scholarly list and Rav Yosef's dilemma exchange; speech without real conflict or action.
A hypothetical legal scenario used to explain the mishna.
An incident only alluded to, cited as precedent for a ruling; not enough of the incident is given.
A man comes before Rabban Gamliel with a claim about his wedding night and the rabbi responds; an incident with a rabbinic response.
Narrated incident: creditor repossesses, purchaser offers payment. Rav Yosef/Abaye's analysis in [4] is commentary, not part of the story.
Rabbi Hanina declines the appointment, sits outside, Rabbi Afes dies, Levi goes to Babylonia and Rav infers the events; a chain of events with consequences.
A halakhic question and answer between Rav Ya'akov bar Avuh and Abaye; speech only, no conflict.
A one-line wonder (fox nesting in a turnip that was weighed), cited as proof; it is the eyewitness-wonder type the expert has accepted, but this one is only marginal.
Rabbis visit the sick Rabba bar bar Hana, a Persian priest takes their lamp, and Rabba responds with an exclamation; events with a reaction.
First-person incidents: a dish was brought before Shmuel / Rav Kahana and they gave the attendant some, saving him from danger; short but narrated events.
Rabbi falls ill, Rabbi Hiyya enters, finds him crying and asks why; a narrated deathbed scene, despite the embedded baraita.
A man snatches coins, throws them to a woman to betroth her, and the case comes before Rava who rules; incident plus ruling.
A poor man eats lentils with Rabbi Nehemya and dies; Nehemya laments. The Gemara's question about his words is commentary but is in the same segment.
A mother writes two deeds, her sons get conflicting rulings from Rav Sheshet and Rav Nahman, who then confront each other; events with conflict.
A report of a habitual practice (a litra of meat daily) with no one-time event following, then Gemara commentary.
Rabbi Tarfon's first-person account: one time he went up to the platform, leaned in, and heard the High Priest hide the Name; an eyewitness incident.
Exegetical and halakhic discussion; Shmuel's instruction to Rav Hana is a bare speech-act cited as evidence.
Purely legal discussion of the grooms' benediction; no narrated event.
A document is brought before Rava, Rav Pappa testifies it was paid, Rava rejects him and is challenged by Rav Adda; courtroom incident with conflict.
Rav Amram, tempted by a captive woman, lifts the ladder, then cries fire, is rebuked by the Sages and expels his evil inclination; a full story.
A city's lineage is contested, Rabbi sends Rabbi Romanus to investigate, and Rabbi rules her fit; incident plus ruling.
Rav Sheila permits a drowned man's wife, Rav wants to excommunicate him, they send to him, he admits error, and Rav and Shmuel praise each other.
A priest marries a young convert, Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak confronts him and orders him to divorce her under threat; incident with conflict and ruling.
A man studies twelve years, his wife becomes infertile, Rabbi deliberates, the husband prays and she is healed; narrated events with a resolution.
An alluded-to incident (Rav Yosef ruled per Rav, Shmuel took offense) cited as evidence in a sugya; there is conflict, but the event is barely narrated.
A certain man gives a conditional divorce, and after thirty days claims he tried; an actual incident that the Gemara goes on to analyze legally.
Transmission of a tradition and its variant; speech only, without conflict.
A report that a difficulty went unresolved for twenty-two years until Rav Yosef resolved it; scholarly report, no narrated incident.
A report of Rabbi Yehuda bar Elai's habitual practice cited to support a baraita; no one-time event follows.
A certain man faces a levirate obligation abroad, comes to Rabbi Hanina, and receives a pointed ruling; an incident with a rabbi's response.
Rabbi falls ill, Rabbi Hiyya visits and finds him weeping, and Rabbi explains his tears; a narrated event with emotion.
A man contests a field and dies; his steward argues before Abaye, wins, and Abaye praises him. An incident followed by rulings and a response.
A Mishnah legal case with a dispute; hypothetical law, no narrated event.
A statement that Rabba and Abaye descended from Eli and how long they lived, cited as evidence for their dicta; a report, not an incident with a response.
Rabbi Asi's relative seeks rulings from two rabbis, gets conflicting answers, and Rabbi Asi confronts Rabbi Yohanan; events with conflict and response.
The Gemara's explanation of what Rabbi Akiva was thinking; commentary on a story, not the story.
A student mocks Rabbi Tarfon's caution and soon after stumbles into sin; an event with a consequence.
Mostly dialogue in which Abaye mocks Rav Pappa as an orphan, plus a bare report of oil smeared at a wedding; speech with conflict but little action.
A fisherman is trapped in a cave, presumed dead, and returns to find his own eulogy; Rabbi draws a lesson. A full narrated incident.
Rami bar Yehezkel visits Benei Berak, sees the wonder of milk and honey mixing, and responds with a verse; an eyewitness wonder incident.
Abdan's daughters-in-law rebel, Rabbi sends Sages, the women retort, and Rabbi rules; an incident followed by a ruling.
A Mehoza woman comes before Rav Nahman, who recognizes her accent and rules, is challenged, and reverses; incident with ruling.
Rav Nahman visits Sura and answers halakhic questions; a legal Q&A with no event beyond speech and no real conflict.
Pure legal discussion of wedding celebration days; no narrated event.
A document from Shmuel's court cited as evidence of his legal view, with the Gemara's explanation; a report, not a story.
Someone sought to give more than a fifth to charity and his colleague prevented him; an act met by another's response.
A woman signs her property to her daughter to keep it from her husband, then marries and is divorced; a narrated incident opening a legal case.
Rav Asi leaves his senile mother, she follows, he consults rabbis, sets out, and learns of her death; a full story.
Legal reasoning about sustenance obligations; no narrated event.
A steward's conduct and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's silence, cited as evidence of his legal view; nothing follows.
Homa comes before Rava, her arm is uncovered, Rava goes home, and his wife drives Homa out of Mehoza; a full story.
The bar Tzartzur heirs come before Rav Amram, ignore his advice, are threatened and sent to Rav Nahman for a ruling; incident with conflict and ruling.
Ilfa hangs from a ship's mast vowing to answer any challenge, an old man challenges him, and he succeeds; a dramatic incident.
Rabbi Hanina bar Pappa's death: the Angel of Death's visits, the delay, the pillar of fire, and Rabbi Alexandri's plea that makes it disappear. A chain of actions with consequences.
Ravina finds Mar bar Rav Ashi braiding a garland and challenges him. One act and a halakhic exchange: there is a mild challenge, but little happens.
Rava's retraction and Rav Mesharshiyya's sarcastic retort are speech and quasi-speech acts only. There is conflict, so borderline.
A case comes before Abaye and is resolved by trickery, with Rav Pappa's intervention. It ends with Abaye's gaze and the death of Rav Pappa's parents: real events and consequences.
The Rabbis urge Rav Sheshet to marry and he deflects them in words; his impotence is only alluded to, as the Gemara's explanation. No narrated event and no real conflict.
Two incidents with responses: a death is reported and the question raised, and a found bill of divorce is sent to Rabbi Yehuda Nesia, who rules. Incident plus ruling.
A man leaves Pumbedita and Rav Yosef excommunicates him; another leaves and dies, and Abaye comments. Something happens and someone responds.
Rabbi Elazar ascends to the Land, is ordained, then joins the intercalation council, reacting at each stage. A sequence of events with change.
Shimon HaAmasoni reaches a verse and withdraws from his method of exposition; his students question him and he answers, and later Rabbi Akiva resolves it. Events with change and a response.
Rabbi Elazar considers a ruling and Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim objects. Quasi-speech with some conflict, and no action.
A ma'aseh: a woman before an unsuitable yavam, a conditional halitza, and Rabbi Hiyya validates it. Incident plus ruling; segment 2 is legal exposition.
A dispute over deposited sesame comes before the Sages, who debate the ruling. Something happened to someone and the court responds.
A divorcee comes before Shmuel; Rav Dimi tests whether the baby recognizes her, the child does, and she is told to take her son. Clear actions and a resolution.
One partner frees half a slave and the other transfers him to his minor son to evade the court. Rav Pappa responds with a scheme. Incident plus ruling.
Eyewitness wonders: 'once I rose early and walked in ankle-deep honey'. The register says the expert accepted this kind of Ketubot 111b report in review and lists it, though it remains an open edge.

A promise between brothers over a yevama is broken and the case comes to court. It is sent back and forth between sages, Rav Yosef searches the sources, and the inquiry is sent again. Incident plus ruling, with narrated actions throughout.
Levi considers acting on a baraita and Rav tells him the halakha. Quasi-speech only, with no real conflict and no event.
Rav Nahman's relative sells her ketubah, is divorced and dies; the buyers claim from her daughter, and Rav Nahman intervenes. Events and a response.
A betrothal with a stone: Rav Hisda appraises it, the mother protests and he rebuts her, and he cites Yehudit's case, itself an incident. Incident plus ruling.
Rabbi's deathbed pronouncements contain an embedded incident: Bireta DeSatya's fish trapped on Shabbat, an excommunication, and apostasy.
A creditor seizes an ox from the orphans' herdsman, they dispute it, and Rav Nahman rules. Incident plus ruling.
A Mishnah reports that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya expounded in Yavne. A bare report of a speech act, with nothing following.
A teaching exchange where a son corrects his father and Shmuel rebukes the son. Dialogue only, but with interpersonal conflict.
A ma'aseh of a half-free woman whom people abused; the court forced her master to free her. Incident and response.
A man wills a dowry to his daughter, its cost falls, and Rav Idi bar Avin rules on the difference. A minimal incident plus a ruling.
Rabbi's son's marriage arrangements: the bride dies, a new match, the son delays study, returns to an infertile wife, prays and she is cured. Multiple events with change.
The launderer misses Rabbi's funeral, throws himself from a roof and dies, and a Divine Voice responds. A clear narrated event sequence.
A slave flees to Eretz Yisrael, his master pursues him and comes before Rabbi Ami, who rules. Incident followed by ruling.
A man's conditional statement and later contrary claim, used as a legal case and analyzed; only speech, no action or resolution beyond legal discussion.
Habitual dancing practice followed by Rabbi Zeira's criticism and the one-time event of the pillar of fire at Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak's death, vindicating him.
First-person reports of being given food, cited as evidence for a halakhic principle about waiters; nothing follows.
Rabbi Yohanan's relatives come to him about a costly treatment, he advises them, and later regrets having acted as a legal advisor. Incident, response and change.
The Sages rebuke ben Azzai for not marrying and he answers; speech only, but with conflict.
A man sets a divorce condition, arrives but is stopped by the ferry, calls out, and Shmuel rules. Incident followed by ruling.
A widow's son questions Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, who exposes him sarcastically; almost entirely dialogue, with some conflict.
Rav Anan's letter, Rav Huna's insulting reply under threat of excommunication, Rav Sheshet delivering it, Rav Anan going to Mar Ukva: conflict with actions.
A man complains of no hymenal blood, the bride claims Dorketi lineage, Rabban Gamliel investigates her relatives and rules. Incident, investigation and ruling.
A brief report that Rabbi Hiyya taught a ruling in two attributions with differing reception, cited only as evidence about the halakha.
An eyewitness report of Ameimar's silence, cited as evidence that he retracted his opinion; nothing develops.
Rabbi's death: the Sages' fast and decree, the maidservant's prayer and thrown jug, his death, bar Kappara's announcement, and Rabbi's final prayer. A full narrative.
A legal dilemma raised by Rabbi Elazar; no event narrated.
An incident in Tzippori is only alluded to as the basis of a ruling; not enough of the incident is given.
Mar Ukva's custom of giving charity is followed by a one-time event: his son reports the pauper's luxury and Mar Ukva doubles the gift.
A man brings Rav Anan a gift, Rav Anan disqualifies himself, accepts it after the man's explanation, and sends him to Rav Nahman, who draws a conclusion. Actions and consequences.
Parents quarrel over whom their daughter will marry, the father yields, and his relative betroths her from the roof during the meal. Abaye's and Rava's analysis that follows is commentary.
Silk is deposited with Rav Dimi, he dies without instructions, the depositor comes before Rabbi Abba, who rules. Incident followed by ruling.
Relatives bring complaints about the orphans' steward Amram before Rav Nahman, who responds and rules on what is needed to remove him. Incident brought to court and resolved.
In Sidon a tanner died and his brother, also a tanner, was due to marry the widow; the Sages ruled she may refuse. Incident and ruling, though it is the Mishnah itself.
Two Sages are about to act on a baraita when an old woman intervenes, recounting an alluded incident where Rav Nahman forbade it; mostly speech with an implied change of course.
A Sadducee's remark to Rabbi Hanina praising his land's yield; speech only, without real conflict or action.
Rav Hiyya bar Abba's child dies; Reish Lakish comes with his disseminator who speaks words of comfort. Segment 4 is the Gemara's commentary on the incident.
A yevama comes for halitza; Abaye hands over his left sandal and Rav Yosef corrects him - a concrete incident with action and response.
At Rabbi's funeral a Divine Voice speaks; the launderer who missed it throws himself from the roof and dies, and a second Divine Voice responds.
Habitual prayer frames a one-time event: his wife disguises herself as a prostitute, he sins, then sits in the oven and fasts for the rest of his life.
A legal discussion of a dispute between Rav and Shmuel about a deathbed gift; no narrated event.
Rav Hamnuna is sent to Rav Huna, who sees his uncovered head, learns he is unmarried, turns his face away and rebukes him - action plus conflict.
An incident: a woman raised a child who later had intercourse with her, and the court stoned them - an event followed by a ruling.
The ill Madonite asks how to give his property, buys land, makes the gift, dies, and the Sages carry out his words.
A man deposited a goblet with Hasa, who died without instructions; they came before Rav Nahman, who ruled - incident plus ruling.
Rabbi Yohanan's relatives seek rulings from Rabbi Yohanan and from Reish Lakish, who threatens them, and they go back to Rabbi Yohanan - a sequence of events with conflict.
A groom complains to Rabban Gamliel, who investigates the bride's family and rules. Segment 3 is later commentary on the incident.
An Arab woman brings tefillin, Abaye makes a lowball offer, she angrily throws them into the river, and Abaye regrets it.
Rabbi Zeira crosses the Jordan on a rope, a Sadducee mocks him, and he replies - an action with conflict and a response.
Ulla visits and sees the unmarried son, but the rest is dialogue with mild conflict; segments 3-5 are interpolated exegesis.
Avimi's habitual honoring of his father frames a one-time event: he stands bent over his dozing father until he wakes, and is rewarded.
The Neresh incident: a bride is seized from her husband and Rav's students do not require a divorce - an event plus a ruling. Segment 3 is the Gemara's analysis.
A man with a conditional divorce arrives on time but is stopped by the ferry, shouts across the river, and Shmuel rules - incident plus ruling.
Segment 2 concludes Rabbi Hanina bar Pappi's story; segment 3 is Rabbi Tzadok's: a noblewoman seduces him, he sits in the oven, and she relents.
Rabbi's deathbed scene and its sequels: he returns on Shabbat eves until a neighbor learns of it, and his attendants die before him. Segments 3-5 and 9 are Gemara commentary.
The conclusion of an incident: his friends shun him, and Rabbi elevates him to the priesthood on his statement - a narrated event with a ruling.
A history of a rabbinic enactment about cups of wine in a house of mourning, not a narrated incident involving particular people.
Elijah's advice to Rabbi Natan is speech alone, with no event or conflict.
Rabbi Yannai rebukes Rav Hanina and orders him out - speech with conflict but no further action.
Only a halakhic question Rabbi Elazar put to an elder about an incident that is alluded to, not narrated.
A general practice of soldiers in David's wars and a verse's exegesis; no narrated event.
Mar Ukva's secret charity: the pauper pursues them, they hide in the furnace, his legs are singed and his wife explains. A full narrative with action and consequence.
Two narrated incidents: a man drowned and was recovered days later, and a rabbi permitted the wife to remarry. An incident followed by a ruling.
A narrative about Nebuchadnezzar, Pelatiah ben Benaiah and the prophet Ezekiel. These are biblical-era characters, not rabbis.
A sharecropper betrothed a woman with stolen onions and came before Rava, who ruled. An incident followed by a ruling; the closing comment is commentary.

Two first-person incidents: food was brought to a rabbi, the attendant was in danger from craving, and the rabbi gave him some. Something happens and a person responds, though it is cited as evidence.
Legal argument between Rav Yosef and Abaye over a mishna. No narrated event.
A Jew and a gentile walking together: the gentile reminds him of the Temple's destruction to slow him, he sighs but keeps pace, and they exchange words. Action with conflict.
A report of Rav's habitual practice of supporting orphan girls, followed by legal analysis. Nothing follows from the act.
A man sold land to Rav Pappa, then no longer needed the money, and Rav Pappa returned the land. An incident with a response.
The husband travelled, spent his own money, took one dinar of hers and came before Rabbi Ami, who ruled and was challenged by the Rabbis. An incident followed by a ruling.
A bare report of how many blessings Levi and Rav Asi recited at weddings, cited as evidence of practice. Nothing follows.
Ilfa hangs from a ship's mast and vows to fall if he cannot answer; an old man comes and challenges him. Dramatic action and a challenge.
The incident is only alluded to: they came before Rabbi Ami and he ruled. Not enough of the incident is given.
Legal discussion: an objection from a mishna and Rava's reinterpretation. No event.
The Gemara's commentary on the story of the son who fell, asking whether it happened and whether he sinned. Commentary, not the story.

Rabbi Abba buys land Rav Giddel was negotiating for; complaints follow, there is a confrontation at the festival, a gift is offered and refused, and the land becomes 'the land of the Sages'. A full narrative.
The Mishnah's incident in Sidon: a tanner died, his brother was also a tanner, and the Sages ruled the widow could refuse. It is a story, but a Mishnah one.
A dying man and his bill of divorce: Rava rules, Rav Ilish objects, Rava is embarrassed, then the facts are revealed and Rava rules again. The final segment is the Gemara's commentary.
Dama ben Netina gives up profit rather than wake his father, and is rewarded with a red heifer. He is a post-biblical figure, so it is in scope.
A pauper demands fine food from Rava and justifies it; Rava's sister then arrives with that very food and Rava concedes. Conflict, an event and a resolution.
Rabbi Oshaya stays silent at Rabbi Yohanan's question, answers Reish Lakish, and is challenged by Rabbi Yehuda Nesia. Mostly speech and quasi-speech acts, but with conflict.
Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi on his deathbed summons the Sages, they enter, and he gives his final instructions. Part of the narrative of his death.
Rabbi Akiva and ben Kalba Savua's daughter: secret betrothal, the father's expulsion and vow, twelve years of study, and his return. A full narrative.
After the custom comes a one-time event: the sharecropper brings fruit early because he has a case. Rabbi Yishmael refuses it and recuses himself, then finds himself biased anyway.
A man frames his wife with egg white to avoid paying her ketubah; Bava ben Buta exposes it, and the man is flogged and made to pay. Abaye's question afterward is commentary.
Rabbi Ami declares a neighbor a mamzer, the man weeps, and Rabbi Ami responds; an incident with reaction and resolution.
Rav Amram is afflicted by the Exilarch's household, tricks them into bringing the right remedy, and Yalta then treats him in the bathhouse; a sequence of events with conflict.
A certain man set a condition on a divorce, was stopped by the ferry, called out, and Shmuel ruled; an incident followed by a ruling.
A scholar reports a teaching to another, who corrects its attribution; transmission of a dictum with no event beyond speech and no real conflict.
A man comes before Rav Nahman with a claim and Rav Nahman orders him flogged; something happens and a rabbi responds with a ruling.
A report of a standing practice (daily meat for a poor man) with nothing following, then the Gemara's commentary on it.
Rav Sheizevi's statement is mocked and Rava rebukes the mockers; speech only, but with conflict.
A general dictum about schooling and its harmonization; no event.
Seizure of a deceased debtor's boat, rival seizures by two rabbis, challenge by Rav Pinehas, and Rava's rebuke and ruling; a full incident with conflict and resolution.
A legal objection from a mishna and its resolution; no narrated event.
A brief exchange of insults between two men, cited as evidence; speech only but with conflict.
Two rabbis intend to act on a baraita and an old woman stops them by recounting her own case where Rav Nahman prohibited it; segment 3 is Gemara discussion.
The Sages apportion wine to Nakdimon's daughter-in-law, she blesses them, and they decline to answer amen; events with a response.
Legal discussion of Abba Shaul's view; the incident in segment 5 is only alluded to, not narrated.
A woman raises a child who later has relations with her, and the court stones them; an incident followed by a court's action.
A single report that a gift of fabrics was sent to Rabbi, followed by glosses on the fabric terms; nothing follows.
Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba encounters R. Yehoshua ben Levi hurrying his grandson to synagogue, questions him, and changes his own practice thereafter.
Solomon, Benayahu, and the capture of Ashmedai: a full story about biblical figures.
Ulla dies abroad, Rabbi Elazar is told and laments, is told the coffin is coming, and responds; events with reactions.
A man comes before Rav Nahman and Rav Nahman orders him flogged; segment 3 is Gemara discussion of the ruling.
Rabbis visit a place and share a giant peach; a year later Rabbi Elazar finds it shrunken and responds with a verse; events with change.
A man rents out a millstone, grows rich, buys his own, and a dispute arises over payment; an incident that the Gemara then rules on.
A report of Hasa's drowning, Rav Nahman's exclamation, and Hasa's wife remarrying unchallenged; segment 3 is an alternate version with Gemara commentary.
A beautiful woman fends off unworthy suitors by claiming betrothal, later betroths herself, and explains herself to the Sages; events with conflict and resolution.
A one-line wonder report (a fox nested in a turnip, which was weighed), the eyewitness-wonder edge that the expert has accepted elsewhere on Ketubot 111b; low confidence.
Legal exposition of the mishna's wording; no narrated event.
A Roman courts a woman, makes her ill with pomegranates, then cures her and she agrees to marry: multiple actions with change, post-biblical figures.
Ravnai arrives and reports a teaching, Ameimar praises it and Rav Ashi rebukes him; essentially speech with some conflict and little action.
A man approaches and kisses Rabbi Yonatan's foot, prompting an exchange explaining that Rabbi Yonatan forced the sons to support him: a narrated incident.
A certain man's creditor repossesses one mansion then seeks the other; the purchaser goes with money and makes an offer: an incident that leads to a ruling.
Purely analytical Gemara discussion of the difference between two opinions.
An incident: Rabbi rules (or intends to), Perata objects, and Rabbi reverses; action, conflict and change, told in two versions.
Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai meets the impoverished daughter of Nakdimon gathering barley from dung; dialogue, recognition, and his weeping: a full story.
Rav Asi leaves his senile mother, hears she is following, consults Rabbis, sets out and meets her coffin: multiple actions with a turn.
A report of Rav Yehuda's ruling with an incident only alluded to; nothing narrated.
Rabba bar bar Hanna's eyewitness account: the Arab woman throws down her spindle, addresses him, and Rav Ukva comments; actions and response.
An agent prevented by circumstances comes before Rava, who rules; the Sages challenge him, he is embarrassed, and it is revealed the woman was only betrothed: incident, ruling, conflict, resolution.
The Nasi's household seizes an orphans' maidservant; the judges approve and Rabbi Abba objects that they flatter the Nasi: an incident with a court response and conflict.
A bachelor comes before Rav Nahman with a claim and Rav Nahman orders him flogged: an incident followed by a rabbi's response.
Rav Hiyya bar Abba's child dies and Reish Lakish comes to comfort him, having his disseminator speak; the Gemara's commentary and Abaye's remarks (3, 4, 7) are not part of the story.
A bare report that Rav Pappa instructed Pappa the ox herder, cited as precedent; nothing follows.
A husband gives his first wife's maidservant to his second wife; she comes crying before Rava, who ignores her: incident and response.
A rumor about a betrothal and Rava's ruling to suppress it; too little of an incident is given, essentially a legal case.
The Nasi's household seizes an orphans' maidservant; the judges approve and Rabbi Abba objects: incident with court response and conflict.
An incident is only alluded to; the content is a legal derivation from a mishna.
Rami bar Hama's mother deeds her property twice; two judges rule for different sons and Rav Sheshet confronts Rav Nahman: incident, rulings, conflict.
Rabbi Pinhas plans his escape, makes his statements, is carried off and pursued, and the investigation is abandoned: multiple actions.
Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai's escape from Jerusalem and meeting with Vespasian; segment 11 is Gemara commentary on his choice.
A man testifies before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, is questioned, and the rabbi elevates the person to Levite status: incident followed by a ruling.
A widow claiming her ketuba dresses in all her clothes at the orphans' request, and Ravina rules they are appraised: incident, action, ruling.
A specific incident: a woman obligated to swear, Rav Hisda's daughter testifies she is suspect, and Rava reverses the oath. Incident plus ruling.
Habitual practice of Rav Safra and Rava cited as evidence for the mitzva; no one-time event follows.
The sharecropper brings fruit early, Rabbi Yishmael refuses it and recuses himself, then catches himself favouring the man and reacts. One-time event after a habitual frame, with a response.
A man appropriated orphans' coral, it appreciated, and he came before Rabbi Ammi who ruled. Incident followed by a ruling.
Continuation of Rav Pappa forcing Yehuda bar Mareimar to enter; his silence leads Abba of Sura to write away all his property, with a resolution. Actions, misunderstanding and consequence.
A betrothed couple came before Rava, he placed an intermediary between them, and Rav Adda challenged him. Incident with a ruling; segment 3 is an alternate version of the same incident.
Agents sent for a silver vessel are pressured, one is beaten, and Rabbi Ahai judges their conduct. Multiple actions, conflict and resolution.
Rav and Rav Yehuda walking behind a woman; Rav urges him to hurry away, and a pointed exchange follows. An actual event with action and conflict.
Describes what the emperor's maidservants used to sing whenever Rabbi Abbahu came; habitual custom with no one-time event.
A city of slaves sold to gentiles, their masters die, they come before Ravina who rules and is challenged. Incident followed by a ruling.
Rabbi Zeira's sermon causes the crowd to pelt him with etrogim; Rava preaches, is carried on silk, then preaches again and is rebuked. Actions and reactions.
An incident (the Yavne reservoir found deficient) followed by the dispute of Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva over it, ending with Tarfon's concession. Incident with resolution.
A bill of divorce turns up in Rav Huna's court, Rav Huna rules, Rav Hisda sends Rabba to investigate, and he goes and finds the source. Incident with actions and a response.
The incident is only alluded to in a sentence of legal summary; not enough of it is narrated.
A baraita recounting an actual incident: the daughters reached Jerusalem before the sons, and they were judged eager and lazy. The register lists Gittin 25a as high confidence.
A man snatches coins, throws them to a woman to betroth her, and the case comes before Rava, who rules. Incident plus ruling.
Rabbi Hanina's habitual charity, then one day his wife delivers it, discovers the pauper's luxury, and he responds. A habitual frame followed by a one-time event.
Marta bat Baitos sends repeatedly for flour, goes out herself, and dies; Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai responds with a verse. Segment 4's alternate version is part of the narrative.
Elijah leaves Rav Anan after his fault, Rav Anan fasts and prays, Elijah returns frightening, and Rav Anan builds a box. Elijah appearing to a rabbi reads as in scope.
He studies twelve years, his wife becomes infertile, Rabbi deliberates, and he prays and she is cured. Event, problem and resolution.
Rav Aha bar Yaakov is afflicted, hung from the cedar post and healed, and he comments on the sixty elders. Something happened and there was a response; the opening list of names is report only.
Rabbi Yohanan's relatives seize orphans' cow and go back and forth between Rabbi Yohanan and Reish Lakish, with a resolution. Incident with rulings and conflict.
A one-line anecdote illustrating a folk belief: Shapur's daughter was fragrant and used to be placed among spices. A habitual result with no event that leads anywhere.
A husband travels to collect his wife's inheritance, spends money and takes one dinar, and comes before Rabbi Ami, who rules and is challenged. Incident followed by a ruling.
Rav Yosef acted on Rav's view and Shmuel took offense with a sarcastic remark: an action and an emotional response. Segment 3 is the Gemara's speculation, not the story.

A certain man's creditor repossessed one mansion; the purchaser offered him a thousand dinars and Rava ruled on the case. That is an incident followed by a ruling. The legal discussion that comes after it is left out.
Pure legal exegesis about a yavam and teruma. Nothing happens in it.
A certain man threw a bill of divorce to his wife, it landed on a board, and Rav Yosef ruled. That is an incident followed by a ruling.
Funeral costs were so heavy that relatives abandoned their dead, until Rabban Gamliel had himself buried in plain linen and everyone followed. There is a problem, an action and a change.
Rabbi Natan asking Sumakhos a legal question and hearing his answer is speech only, with no conflict and no event.

Embedded in Rabbi Abbahu's dictum is an incident: a great man imposed excessive fear on his household, and they fed him something forbidden. The Gemara's identification and revision that follow are commentary, so they are excluded.
The Tzaidan incident is only alluded to ("etc."). The segment is the Gemara's question about why the mishna cites it.
Her marriage contract was lost, the couple came before Rav Yosef, and he responded with a ruling. That is an incident and a response.
A man insults Rav Yehuda, is excommunicated and declared a slave, and summons Rav Yehuda before Rav Nahman. A tense encounter follows, so there are multiple actions and conflict.
A report that a legal difficulty went unresolved for 22 years until Rav Yosef resolved it. It frames the legal answer and has no narrative development.
A hypothetical legal case ("where the father delivered..."), not an event that happened.
After the habitual frame of Rabbi's Shabbat-eve visits comes a one-time event: the maid silenced a neighbor, and he never came again.
Rav Hiyya bar Abba's child died; Reish Lakish came the next day with his disseminator, who spoke words of comfort. These are actions in response to an event.
These are brief first-person reports that a teacher shared his food, cited as evidence for a practice. Nothing develops from them.
Rabbi Akiva and Ben Kalba Savua's daughter is a full narrative: a secret betrothal, a father's vow, decades of study, a return, and a reconciliation.
From Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's habitual practice the passage moves to a one-time event: he tricks the Angel of Death, enters paradise, and meets Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai.
Dama ben Netina's mother tore his cloak, struck him and spat at him, and he did not embarrass her. There are actions and a response, and he is a post-biblical figure.
What Ravina did in collecting for Rav Ashi's daughter is cited as legal evidence. No incident is narrated.
On his deathbed Rabbi summons his sons; each enters, and he hands over wisdom and the office of Nasi. These are actions within a larger narrative.
A fragment of exegesis about the omer. It is not a narrative.
A report of Rav Kahana's practice in delaying the sale of an orphan's beer, cited as legal evidence. Nothing follows from it.
Shimon HaAmasoni's habitual exegesis is followed by a one-time event: he withdrew at one verse, his students challenged him, and he answered.
A sharecropper betrothed a woman with stolen onions, came before Rava, and Rava ruled. That is an incident followed by a ruling.
A man deposited pearls with Rabbi Meyasha, who died without instructions; the parties came before Rabbi Ami, who ruled. That is an incident followed by a ruling.
Rav Pappa intended to rule, was challenged by Rav Huna, and desisted. The exchange is mostly speech, but there is conflict and a change.

After the Beitar custom comes a one-time event: the emperor's daughter's shaft breaks, a cedar is cut, the residents beat her attendants and the emperor attacks. Segments 3-4 are exegesis and descriptions of the aftermath.
Rabbi Meir mocks transgressors, Satan appears as a woman, he crosses the rope bridge and Satan lets go of him: a full narrative with actions and a turn.
Legal explanation of a government decree and the Sages' reasoning; no narrated incident about particular people.

An incident: the ill mother of the sons of Rokhel gave her brooch to her daughter, died, and the Sages carried out her statement, after which Rabbi Elazar curses the sons. Segment 2 is a quoted mishna.
Purely halakhic discussion of converting a minor; nothing is narrated.
A man says where he is from and Rabbi Yitzhak locates the place; this is speech without conflict, followed by legal discussion.
Ulla dies abroad, Rabbi Elazar is told and laments, they say his coffin is coming, and he replies: an event and a response.
Rav Sheshet flogging a son-in-law is only alluded to, as evidence in a legal discussion of Rav's floggings; too little of the incident is given.
Ilfa's incident: a man lovesick for a woman wanted to leave the Land, heard this teaching, and stayed and suffered until he died. Segments 3-4 are advice in a letter.
A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, Rav Dimi died, and Rabbi Abba ruled: an incident followed by a ruling.
The dispute over Rav Giddel's land: complaints, a confrontation at the festival, the offer of a gift, both refuse it, and it comes to be called the land of the Sages.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's curse on Gavla's huge grape clusters, and its fulfilment the next year when Rabbi Hiyya visits.
Gardeners settle accounts, one gardener later finds he owed nothing, and Rav Nahman rules: an incident followed by a ruling.
Dama ben Netina, a post-biblical figure, does not wake his father and is rewarded with a red heifer; a full narrative.
Bar Shatya sold property, two pairs of witnesses contradicted each other, and Rav Ashi ruled: a narrated incident with a ruling, though it is thin.
A document is brought before Rava, Rav Pappa testifies that it was paid, Rava rejects his lone testimony, and Rav Adda challenges him: a court incident with a ruling and conflict.
A habitual 'when such a case came before Rava he would say', with no one-time event; speech only.
A real situation (a yevama falls to a man) brings a question and Rabbi Hanina's sharp rebuke, but there is no action beyond the speech.
Two deeds come before Rav Yosef, who rules, and the losing claimant protests: an incident with a ruling and conflict.
A narrated incident: the debtor sells his mansions, the creditor repossesses one and then goes after the other, and the purchaser responds with an offer.
A widow comes before Rav Huna, is refused, takes an oath on her own initiative, and Rav Huna rules in her favour.
Rabbi Pinhas plans his statements, delivers them, is carried off on a stretcher and chased, and the investigation that follows is abandoned.
Exegetical discussion of bar Kappara's teaching, with an objection and answers; no events.
Sages reclining together have a discussion and reach a conclusion, like the Yevamot 17a seating; no action follows.
Rabbi's deathbed instructions, his Shabbat-eve visits and their end, and the deaths of his attendants form a narrative. Segments 3-5 and 9 are the Gemara's commentary.
A certain man sent a get; the wife told the agent to hold it; rabbis dispute and send the case up to Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba. An incident followed by rulings.
After the habitual frame, a one-time event follows: Yehuda is delayed, Rabbi Yannai declares him dead, and Yehuda dies.
A bare report of the blessing Rav Haviva recited, cited as his practice and followed by a halakhic ruling. Nothing happens after it.
Ze'eiri avoids Rabbi Yohanan, then carries him across water, and is confronted about the marriage. Actions, conflict and dialogue.
A post-biblical (Destruction-era) incident: the captive priest's daughter is abused, put up for sale, and protests to God. The Jeremiah lament in [5] is commentary.
The blind man is late, the messenger reports adultery, and Mar Shmuel rules. An incident followed by a ruling.
Rava and his wife exchange words about the Sages' gossip. It is speech alone, but with conflict.
The bathhouse and the stair collapse; the rabbis pull their supporters up, and the Sages question Rabbi Yohanan. Events with a response.
A widow comes before Rav Nehemya with demands and he rules on them. A court incident with a ruling.
The incident is only alluded to (Rabbi gave one-twelfth) as evidence in a legal argument. Too little of the incident is given.
Orphans' property is held by Rabbi Banai; they come before Shmuel, who orders support. Brief, but an incident with a ruling.
Rami bar Yehezkel visits Benei Berak, witnesses the wonder and responds. The eyewitness-wonder type the expert accepted.
The Kamtza and bar Kamtza narrative, a post-biblical story with many actions and consequences. Rabbi Yohanan's comment in [8] is commentary.
Rav's examination of a family is only alluded to as evidence in a halakhic argument.
Rabbi recounts how Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua's students ganged up on him and stopped him studying. Conflict, with a consequence.
The King Yannai baraita: the feast, the slander, the expulsion and the killing of the Sages. A post-biblical figure, so in scope.
Rabban Gamliel serves at his son's wedding; Rabbi Eliezer refuses the cup, Rabbi Yehoshua accepts it, and they dispute. Action plus conflict.
The refusal by Pishon's wife is only alluded to inside a dispute between Beit Hillel and Beit Shammai. Not enough of the incident is given.

An incident that happened to a girl in Hitlu (a dog attacked her while sweeping) followed by Rabbi's ruling; R-C0 says an incident followed by a ruling can be a story, and this is not merely a report of someone's practice.
A purely legal debate about the Festival and Shabbat. No narrated event.
The extended narrative of the Nehardean man, Rav Yehuda's excommunication, the summons before Rav Nahman, and the aftermath in Neharde'a.
An institutional history of how the court changed an ordinance, given as Rav Ashi's legal explanation. No particular incident or characters.
After the habitual charity frame, one day the pauper pursues them; Mar Ukva and his wife hide in a furnace, with dialogue and an emotional reaction.
Rav Ashi's daughter is ill, Ravin treats her, and she is healed. Something happens to someone and a person responds.
A certain man betrothed a girl with vegetables in the market and Ravina ruled. The incident-plus-ruling shape.

A man deposited pearls, the custodian died without instructions, and the parties came before Rabbi Ami, who ruled: an incident resolved by a ruling. Segment 3 is the Gemara's qualification, not part of the story.
Rav Yitzhak bar Yosef found Rabbi Abbahu at Usha, asked who taught the halakha, then learned it from him forty times until it was fixed in his memory: a narrated event that goes beyond speech.
Rabbis visit a place and are served a giant peach; a year later Rabbi Elazar finds it shrunk and responds with a verse. Events, change and a reaction.
During a drought everyone in Neharde'a sold their mansions, then wheat arrived and Rav Nahman ruled the sales void: an incident followed by a ruling.
A man recalls being immersed to eat teruma and mocked by friends, and Rabbi elevates him to the priesthood on his word: an incident with a resolution.
The wedding custom at Tur Malka is the frame. A one-time event follows (Romans seize the chickens, a revolt, bar Deroma, his death, the massacre): a full story about post-biblical figures.
A man mortgaged his orchard, it aged after five years, and the creditor came before the Sages, who wrote him an authorization: an incident with a ruling.
Rabbi Yosei travels to Netzivin and questions an elder. Almost entirely dialogue, but with a disagreement over the halakha, so it is speech with some conflict.
Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai meets Nakdimon's impoverished daughter, recalls her ketuba and weeps: a full story. Segment 5 is the Gemara's question about it.
Rav Huna tore silk garments in front of his son to test whether he would get angry: a narrated action with intent. The Gemara's questions after it are commentary.
Gentiles went about announcing the deaths of Hivvai and of a horseman, and Rav Yosef let the wives remarry: incidents resolved by rulings.
This is the opening clause of an incident (a man's will, a change in the wine's value, Rav Yosef's ruling); the passage is the start of that incident-plus-ruling story.
Rabbi Elazar goes up to the Land of Israel, is ordained and is seated in the intercalation council, reacting at each stage: a sequence of events that happened to him.
A halakhic dispute and a baraita about teruma rations. No narrated event.
A husband gave one of his first wife's maidservants to his new wife, she cried out before Rava, and he ignored her: an incident with a response.
Analysis of the Mishnah's wording. No event.
A man came before Rabbi Ami about another man's priestly status, and Rabbi Ami questioned him and elevated that man to the priesthood: an incident resolved by a ruling.
Gentiles announced men's deaths offhandedly, and Rav Yosef (or Rava) allowed the wives to marry: incidents followed by rulings.
A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the market, the case was sent to Rav Yosef, and he ruled to flog the man and require a get: an incident with a ruling.
Incidents in which a gentile reported Jewish travellers dead and buried, and the Sages let their wives remarry: events followed by rulings.
A legal dispute between Pumbedita and Mata Mehasya over a hypothetical case. No event.
Mar bar Rav Ashi buying a cloth for more than its value is a bare report cited as evidence; nothing follows from it.
A corpse fragment was found under a boat carrying purification waters on the Jordan, and the Sages issued a decree: an incident with a response.
A man sold his property meaning to move to the Land of Israel without saying so, and Rava ruled the unspoken intention void: an incident followed by a ruling.
During a drought in Neharde'a people sold their mansions, wheat then arrived, and Rav Nahman ruled the mansions return to their owners: an incident with a ruling.
A certain man willed a dowry, its cost fell, and Rav Idi bar Avin ruled on the difference: a narrated incident resolved by a ruling.
A certain man betrothed with a myrtle branch in the market; the case was sent to Rav Yosef, who ordered flogging and a get. Incident plus ruling.
An actual incident in which Rafram pressured Rav Ashi and Rav Ashi collected the full value: events with a response.
Bar Shatya sold property, two pairs of witnesses contradicted each other, and Rav Ashi ruled: an incident followed by a ruling.
Mostly speech: a public teaching, a challenge, and a public retraction through an interpreter. There is conflict and change but little action; the expert ruled Gittin 43a low confidence at most.
A man comes before Rabban Gamliel with a claim and receives a challenging reply and parable. It is essentially dialogue, with some conflict.
Rabbi Hanina refuses the appointment, Rabbi Afes dies, Levi goes to Babylonia, and Rav deduces what happened. Segment 4 is the Gemara's commentary and is excluded.
A marriage contract was brought before Rabbi Abbahu, he meant to validate it, and Rabbi Yirmeya objected: an incident with a response.
The incident is only alluded to ('there was an incident like this'), with not enough of it given to make a story.
Ravina held his orphaned nephew's wine, came to Rav Ashi about taking it to market, and Rav Ashi ruled: incident plus ruling.
A halakhic objection quoting a mishna. Nothing is narrated.
Rabbi Akiva's students die for not respecting one another, and he then teaches new students in the South: narrated events with consequences. Segment 4 is added detail and comment about the deaths.
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi sees the giant clusters and curses the land; the next year the fruit has shrunk and the locals send Rabbi Hiyya away. Events, a reaction and a consequence.
Rabbi Hananya ben Hakhinai leaves for twelve years and returns; his wife dies on seeing him and is revived by his prayer. A full narrative.
Legal discussion of defects in slaves. No event is narrated.
An incident: Levites leave a sick companion at an inn, the innkeeper reports his death, and his wife is permitted to remarry. It is a Mishnah story (R-C1), but a story.
The elders gather in Lod and debate whether study or action is greater, with a resolution. Speech only, but it carries disagreement and a resolution.
Rabbi's son's first match ends when the girl dies, prompting a genealogy check; a second match follows, with the son's changing demands, his shame and his father's reassurance. Narrated events.
A maidservant immersed, a bone was found between her teeth, and Rabbi required her to immerse again: something happened and a rabbi responded.
A sick man in Jerusalem acquired land to transfer his movables, died, and the Sages upheld his words: an incident followed by a ruling.
A man let witnesses trace their names on ordinary documents, and Rav Kahana had him flogged: an act followed by a response.
Rabba bar bar Hana brought a bill of divorce only half written in his presence and came before Rabbi Elazar, who ruled: incident plus ruling.
A habitual prayer frames a one-time event: his wife disguises herself, he sins, he sits in the oven, and he fasts for the rest of his life. A full narrative.
Describes Rabbi Abba's habitual charitable practice with no one-time event and nothing following it.
Legal statements and Gemara analysis about the 'unobstructed orifice' claim. No event is narrated.
Ravin recited the blessing from betrothal, confident the match would hold; it fell through. An event with an outcome, not just a report of practice.
Titus desecrates the Temple, is challenged at sea, tormented by the gnat, and dies. A full narrative about a post-biblical figure; the exegetical interjections are commentary.
Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba witnesses lax practice in Gavla, reports to Rabbi Yohanan, who instructs a public declaration: an incident followed by a ruling.
A report of Rav Kahana's handling of an orphan's beer and his reasoning, with nothing following.
The Mishnah incident is only alluded to by its heading; the passage is Rav's legal derivations from it.
The teacher is absent three days, is questioned, recounts the miraculous harvest, and Reish Lakish responds: events with a response.
Only Abaye's rebuking message to Ravin: speech with conflict but no further action.
A man sets a condition, tries to appease his wife, fails, and Rav Yosef rules: an incident followed by a ruling.
Rav Nahman's relative sells her ketubah, is divorced and dies, the buyers claim from her daughter, and Rav Nahman intervenes.
The death of Rabbi: the fast, the maidservant's prayer and jug, bar Kappara's announcement, his last words. A full narrative.
Two rabbis on the road see men sowing mixed seeds and argue over ostracizing them. Mostly dialogue, with a disagreement but no resulting action.
Rav Aha bar Ya'akov goes to study, is denied lodging, and defeats the seven-headed demon in the study hall: a clear narrative.
Peleimu's habitual taunt frames a one-time event: Satan comes as a pauper on Yom Kippur eve, feigns death, and confronts him.
Rabba bar bar Hana gives Rav money to buy land and Rav buys it for himself: an incident with conflict, which the Gemara then justifies.
A baraita stating a hypothetical legal case, not an event that happened.
The opening of the narrative of the rabbis at King Izgur's gate (sitting, the butler passing, Rav Ashi noticing); the passage is the start of a story.
Incidents that came before Rabbi and Rabbi Yishmael are mentioned only as rulings, without the incident itself; the rest is legal discussion.
Abaye's and Rav Sheshet's practices are reports; the visit to Rav Kahana is a brief challenge and reply, speech with mild conflict.
Shmuel's maidservant is captured, redeemed and sent back with a message about her status: an incident with consequences.
The carpenter's apprentice schemes to take his master's wife, marries her, and humiliates the master: a full narrative.
A woman from Mehoza married into Neharde'a comes before Rav Nahman, who recognizes her accent, rules, and is corrected: an incident with a ruling.
Rav Ashi fails to remember, later remembers and testifies, sees Rav Kahana's hesitation, and reassures him: a sequence of events with a response.
